# snorg

```go
import "github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/pkg/snorg"
```

Package snorg is the public Go API for the supernote\-organizer \(SNORG\): a single facade over an archive of ingested .note files. A Client bundles an archive root with merged configuration and exposes snorg's capabilities — ingest, list, query, retrieve, analyze, export, serve, migrate and programmatic page edits. The snorg CLI \(cmd/snorg\) is itself a consumer of this package.

Construct a Client with Open \(an explicit archive root plus an optional config\) or Resolve \(the CLI's config\-layering and archive\-path fallback\). The internal/\* packages that implement each capability are not importable from outside the module; every type this package returns is re\-exported here \(see types.go\).

```go
const (
    LinkUnknown = snote.LinkUnknown
    LinkNote    = snote.LinkNote
    LinkFile    = snote.LinkFile

)
```

<a name="MigrateCurrent"></a>The MigrateOutcome values, reported per file in a MigrateResult: a file already at CurrentSchemaVersion, or one walked forward to it.

```go

    MigrateCurrent  = archive.MigrateCurrent
    MigrateUpgraded = archive.MigrateUpgraded
)
```

<a name="TextUnchanged"></a>The TextKind values a TextChange.Kind takes; only an edit produces TextReverted.

```go

    TextUnchanged = archive.TextUnchanged
    TextNew       = archive.TextNew
    TextUpdated   = archive.TextUpdated
    TextCleared   = archive.TextCleared
    TextReverted  = archive.TextReverted
)
```

<a name="CurrentSchemaVersion"></a>CurrentSchemaVersion is the archive schema version stamped by every writer; migrate upgrades older files to it.

```go
const CurrentSchemaVersion = archive.CurrentSchemaVersion
```

<a name="QuerySyntax"></a>QuerySyntax summarizes the expression language ParseQuery accepts, for command help and usage errors.

```go
const QuerySyntax = `an expression of terms joined by AND / OR / NOT, grouped with parentheses:
  terms (no value): all, starred, unanalyzed, templated
  terms (with a value): note, keyword, tag, content, region[<box-id>],
    ctime:<spec> (created), mtime:<spec> (modified in the archive), dtime:<spec> (changed on the device)
  operators: ':' substring (case-insensitive), '~' regexp, '=' exact
  time <spec>: today | yesterday | YYYY-MM-DD | FROM..TO (either end may be empty)
  a value must follow its operator immediately; quote it if it holds spaces or parens
  example: starred AND (ctime:2026-04-04..2026-09-12 OR content:"some thing")`
```

<a name="MatchTemplated"></a>
## func [MatchTemplated](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/predicate.go#L74>)

```go
func MatchTemplated(p Page) (bool, error)
```

MatchTemplated matches pages drawn on a configured template — a page whose background\_hash resolves to a templates: entry. The resolution is the config's, not the stored analysis', so a page matches before it is ever analyzed; with no templates configured nothing matches, and MatchNot\(MatchTemplated\) is exactly the free\-form pages.

<a name="ParseDateSpec"></a>
## func [ParseDateSpec](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/querylang.go#L174>)

```go
func ParseDateSpec(spec string) (from, to time.Time, err error)
```

ParseDateSpec turns a ctime/mtime/dtime term's value into an inclusive \[from, to\] range of days for MatchCreated/MatchModified/MatchDeviceModified, each at midnight \(a zero bound is open\). It accepts "today"/"yesterday" \(local time\), a single "YYYY\-MM\-DD" day, and "FROM..TO" ranges with either end omitted.

<a name="AnalysisConfig"></a>
## type [AnalysisConfig](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/types.go#L27>)

Config and its nested sections, as loaded from YAML by LoadConfig. A section alias carries a Config suffix wherever the bare name is taken by something else: ExportConfig/IngestConfig next to the Client.Export/Client.Ingest operations, AnalysisConfig next to PageAnalysis, ProviderConfig next to the Provider interface \(analyze.go\), and TemplateConfig/BoxConfig next to the resolved Template/Box below.

```go
type AnalysisConfig = config.Analysis
```

<a name="AnalyzeOptions"></a>
## type [AnalyzeOptions](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/analyze.go#L47-L56>)

AnalyzeOptions tunes a batch analysis.

```go
type AnalyzeOptions struct {
    Force bool  // re-analyze even pages whose fingerprint is unchanged (blank pages/boxes still cost no call)
    Spec  *Spec // prompts to analyze with; nil = the client's config (AnalyzeSpec)

    // OnResult, when set, is called with each page's result as it lands — before
    // the next page is analyzed — so a caller can log or commit incrementally
    // instead of waiting for the whole batch. It runs synchronously on the
    // calling goroutine. Every result passed here is also in the returned slice.
    OnResult func(AnalyzeResult)
}
```

<a name="Client"></a>
## type [Client](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/snorg.go#L32-L39>)

Client is a handle on one archive plus its merged configuration. It is meant to be reused; the one piece of cross\-call state is the API key NewProvider resolves, cached so a shell api\_key\_command runs once per client \(which also makes a Client unsafe to share across goroutines\).

```go
type Client struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="Open"></a>
### func [Open](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/snorg.go#L51>)

```go
func Open(archivePath string, cfg *Config) (*Client, error)
```

Open returns a Client for the archive rooted at archivePath. cfg may be nil, in which case built\-in defaults are used \(equivalent to LoadConfig\(nil\)\). The config's ingest.svg toggles are applied to the archive's SVG pipeline, so Ingest honors them; unset toggles keep the default pipeline. cfg should come from LoadConfig \(or nil\) so its defaults are populated.

<a name="Resolve"></a>
### func [Resolve](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/snorg.go#L132>)

```go
func Resolve(opts ResolveOptions) (*Client, error)
```

Resolve builds a Client the way the CLI does: it loads the merged config in increasing precedence \(XDG user config → \-c files, later wins\) in a single pass, then locates the archive root — the ArchivePath option \(CWD\-relative, like any CLI path\), else the archive: key from that merged config \(resolved by config.Load relative to the file that declared it\). A leading \~ is expanded either way.

<a name="Client.Analyze"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [Analyze](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/analyze.go#L87>)

```go
func (c *Client) Analyze(ctx context.Context, prov Provider, pageIDs []string, opts AnalyzeOptions) ([]AnalyzeResult, error)
```

Analyze transcribes each page with prov, skipping unchanged ones unless opts.Force. The caller owns the Provider \(build it once with NewProvider\), so a batch costs no credential setup. Pages are processed sequentially \(LLM rate limits\) and a page failure lands in its AnalyzeResult.Err without aborting the batch; set opts.OnResult to observe results as they land.

A cancelled ctx stops the batch: the results so far are returned with ctx.Err\(\).

<a name="Client.ApplyPage"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [ApplyPage](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/edit.go#L31>)

```go
func (c *Client) ApplyPage(pageID, buffer string) (PageEdit, error)
```

ApplyPage stores an edited page buffer \(as produced by PageBuffer\): the content becomes the effective transcription — its divergence from the AI base is kept so the edit survives re\-analysis — and each changed title/link name becomes a user override. It returns the same PageEdit account as EditPage. A malformed buffer writes nothing.

<a name="Client.EditPage"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [EditPage](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/edit.go#L14>)

```go
func (c *Client) EditPage(pageID, editor string) (PageEdit, error)
```

EditPage is the interactive convenience behind the CLI's analyze\-edit: it opens the page buffer in editor \(a shell command line\) and stores the result. The returned PageEdit says what the round\-trip changed — the content TextChange, the per\-box breakdown on a templated page, and the title/link name overrides. Library callers that do not want to spawn an editor should use PageBuffer \+ ApplyPage.

<a name="Client.Ingest"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [Ingest](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/snorg.go#L241>)

```go
func (c *Client) Ingest(ctx context.Context, paths []string, opts IngestOptions) ([]IngestResult, error)
```

Ingest registers each note path into the archive, running the config's SVG pipeline. Results preserve input order; a note's failure is reported in its IngestResult.Err without aborting the batch.

A cancelled ctx stops the batch: the results so far are returned with ctx.Err\(\).

<a name="Client.Migrate"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [Migrate](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/snorg.go#L291>)

```go
func (c *Client) Migrate(ctx context.Context, pageIDs []string, opts MigrateOptions) ([]MigrateResult, error)
```

Migrate upgrades the given pages \(and their owning notes\) to the current schema version; an empty pageIDs migrates the whole archive \(see MigrateAll\). Per\-file errors are reported in the results, not returned.

A cancelled ctx stops the batch: the results so far are returned with ctx.Err\(\).

```go
func (c *Client) MigrateAll(ctx context.Context, opts MigrateOptions) ([]MigrateResult, error)
```

NewProvider builds the Provider the client's configuration describes, resolving the API key \(api\_key \> api\_key\_command stdout \> $OPENAI\_API\_KEY\). Call it once and reuse the Provider across Analyze calls.

<a name="Client.PageBuffer"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [PageBuffer](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/edit.go#L22>)

```go
func (c *Client) PageBuffer(pageID string) (string, error)
```

PageBuffer renders a page's editable transcription buffer: the per\-region title/ link name header \(only when the page has regions\) plus the current content. It is the non\-interactive form of the CLI's analyze\-edit — no editor is spawned. Feed an edited buffer back to ApplyPage.

<a name="Client.Query"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [Query](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/snorg.go#L168>)

```go
func (c *Client) Query(pred Predicate) ([]Match, error)
```

Query returns the pages matching pred \(see the Match\* constructors and ParseQuery\), each with the note.json and \<PAGEID\>.json documents the walk read. Order follows the archive walk: List order, then note.json page order. The first error a predicate returns aborts the walk and is returned, naming its page, so the result set never mixes matched pages with pages that were never read.

<a name="Client.ReadAnalysis"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [ReadAnalysis](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/snorg.go#L208>)

```go
func (c *Client) ReadAnalysis(pageID string) (string, error)
```

ReadAnalysis returns a page's transcription — the \<PAGEID\>.md sidecar, AI\-produced or hand\-written. A never\-analyzed page reads as empty, not as an error.

<a name="Client.ReadNote"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [ReadNote](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/snorg.go#L184>)

```go
func (c *Client) ReadNote(fileID string) (NoteDoc, error)
```

ReadNote returns the raw note.json document for fileID.

<a name="Client.ReadPage"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [ReadPage](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/snorg.go#L189>)

```go
func (c *Client) ReadPage(pageID string) (PageDoc, error)
```

ReadPage returns the raw \<PAGEID\>.json document. Like every single\-page reader it takes the PAGEID alone \(it names one page in one note\) and wraps ErrNotFound for an unknown one.

<a name="Client.ReadSVG"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [ReadSVG](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/snorg.go#L198>)

```go
func (c *Client) ReadSVG(pageID string) ([]byte, error)
```

ReadSVG returns a page's rendered SVG bytes.

<a name="Client.RenderRegion"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [RenderRegion](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/render.go#L9>)

```go
func (c *Client) RenderRegion(pageID string, rect Rect, styled bool) ([]byte, error)
```

RenderRegion renders rect of a page as PNG bytes in the 1920x2560 page pixel space; Rect\{W: 1920, H: 2560\} is the whole page. styled false is the canonical black\-on\-white crop Analyze sends to the model; true rasterizes the stored SVG as\-is. Neither draws the template background image.

<a name="Client.Retrieve"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [Retrieve](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/snorg.go#L181>)

```go
func (c *Client) Retrieve(pageIDs []string) (*Result, error)
```

Retrieve assembles the given pages into a Result: the absolute archive root plus the pages grouped per owning note in placement order. An unknown PAGEID is an error.

<a name="Client.ServeHandler"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [ServeHandler](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/snorg.go#L275>)

```go
func (c *Client) ServeHandler(res *Result, opts ServeOptions) http.Handler
```

ServeHandler returns the built\-in HTTP viewer over an already\-retrieved Result \(see Retrieve\) as an http.Handler. Binding a listener is left to the caller.

<a name="Client.Tag"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [Tag](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/tag.go#L10>)

```go
func (c *Client) Tag(pageIDs []string, tag string) (int, error)
```

Tag adds tag to each of pageIDs — the snorg\-managed labels that live alongside a page's device keywords. Tags are kept sorted and de\-duplicated on disk. It returns the number of pages actually changed \(a page already carrying the tag writes nothing\); it stops and reports the first error, so an unknown PAGEID aborts the batch.

<a name="Client.TagNote"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [TagNote](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/tag.go#L25>)

```go
func (c *Client) TagNote(fileIDs []string, tag string) (int, error)
```

TagNote adds tag to each of fileIDs — a note\-level snorg tag, stored in that note's note.json only and inherited by every one of its pages \(the pages' own tags are never touched\). It returns the number of notes actually changed; it stops and reports the first error, so an unknown FILE\_ID aborts the batch.

<a name="Client.Tags"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [Tags](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/inventory.go#L11>)

```go
func (c *Client) Tags() ([]ValueCount, error)
```

Tags lists the archive's distinct snorg\-managed tags with per\-value page counts, sorted by value \(the read side of the CLI's \`list tags\`\).

<a name="Client.Templates"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [Templates](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/snorg.go#L219>)

```go
func (c *Client) Templates() *Templates
```

Templates returns the template set built from the config's templates: section, against which a page's BackgroundHash is matched. Open resolved it, so a broken templates: section already failed there.

<a name="Client.Untag"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [Untag](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/tag.go#L17>)

```go
func (c *Client) Untag(pageIDs []string, tag string) (int, error)
```

Untag removes tag from each of pageIDs, like Tag in reverse. A tag the page only inherits from its note is not its own to remove \(see UntagNote\) and counts as unchanged.

<a name="Client.UntagNote"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) [UntagNote](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/tag.go#L30>)

```go
func (c *Client) UntagNote(fileIDs []string, tag string) (int, error)
```

UntagNote removes a note\-level tag from each of fileIDs, like TagNote in reverse.

<a name="Config"></a>
## type [Config](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/types.go#L26>)

Config and its nested sections, as loaded from YAML by LoadConfig. A section alias carries a Config suffix wherever the bare name is taken by something else: ExportConfig/IngestConfig next to the Client.Export/Client.Ingest operations, AnalysisConfig next to PageAnalysis, ProviderConfig next to the Provider interface \(analyze.go\), and TemplateConfig/BoxConfig next to the resolved Template/Box below.


LoadConfig loads and deep\-merges the YAML config files \(later paths override earlier ones\) and applies snorg's built\-in defaults. Pass the result to Open, or pass nil to Open for defaults only.

The ingest change report, reachable as IngestResult.Report: which pages were newly written or changed, which files changed on each, which pages were pruned \(and which of those had their state parked for reclaim\), which pages were adopted from another note the device moved them out of, and which notes that repair rewrote.

<a name="Predicate"></a>
## type [Predicate](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/predicate.go#L38>)

Predicate decides whether a candidate page matches. Client.Query calls one per page of the archive; every Match\* function below builds one, and a hand\-written predicate is just a func of the same shape. A predicate that cannot decide \(a read failed\) returns the error rather than false: Query stops and returns it, since an unreadable page counted as a non\-match is one MatchNot would report as a match.

```go
type Predicate func(Page) (bool, error)
```

<a name="MatchAnd"></a>
### func [MatchAnd](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/predicate.go#L79>)

```go
func MatchAnd(preds ...Predicate) Predicate
```

MatchAnd matches a page only when every predicate does \(empty = matches all\). Used to intersect a filter with a piped candidate set, so query A | query B == A∩B. The first error stops it.

<a name="MatchContent"></a>
### func [MatchContent](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/predicate.go#L212>)

```go
func MatchContent(m TextMatcher) Predicate
```

MatchContent matches pages whose transcription \(Page.Transcription\) matches. A never\-analyzed page reads as empty, so it matches only a matcher that accepts the empty string; an unreadable sidecar is an error, not empty. On a templated page the transcription is the whole region\-section document, markers included — MatchRegion is the per\-box view of the same text.

<a name="MatchCreated"></a>
### func [MatchCreated](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/predicate.go#L163>)

```go
func MatchCreated(from, to time.Time) Predicate
```

MatchCreated matches pages whose creation day \(embedded in the PAGEID\) falls within \[from, to\], both inclusive. Only each bound's calendar day counts \(in its own location; the time of day is ignored\), and a zero bound is open. Pages whose PAGEID carries no date never match.

<a name="MatchDeviceModified"></a>
### func [MatchDeviceModified](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/predicate.go#L180>)

```go
func MatchDeviceModified(from, to time.Time) Predicate
```

MatchDeviceModified matches pages last changed on the device \(new or moved page, handwriting, titles/links/keywords, star, background\) on a local day within \[from, to\]; bounds as in MatchCreated.

<a name="MatchIDs"></a>
### func [MatchIDs](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/predicate.go#L118>)

```go
func MatchIDs(ids []string) Predicate
```

MatchIDs matches pages whose PAGEID is in ids \(an empty set matches nothing\). This is the restriction applied when PAGEIDs are piped into query on stdin.

<a name="MatchKeyword"></a>
### func [MatchKeyword](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/predicate.go#L135>)

```go
func MatchKeyword(m TextMatcher) Predicate
```

MatchKeyword matches pages with at least one device keyword whose text matches.

<a name="MatchModified"></a>
### func [MatchModified](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/predicate.go#L173>)

```go
func MatchModified(from, to time.Time) Predicate
```

MatchModified matches pages last modified in the archive \(any page file changed: re\-ingest, analyze, analyze\-edit, tag\) on a local day within \[from, to\]; bounds as in MatchCreated.

<a name="MatchNot"></a>
### func [MatchNot](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/predicate.go#L106>)

```go
func MatchNot(pred Predicate) Predicate
```

MatchNot matches exactly the pages pred does not \(the inverse of a filter\); an error passes through uninverted. Under piping it combines via MatchAnd, so query A | query NOT B == A minus B.

<a name="MatchNote"></a>
### func [MatchNote](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/predicate.go#L130>)

```go
func MatchNote(m TextMatcher) Predicate
```

MatchNote matches the pages of the notes whose FILE\_ID matches.

<a name="MatchOr"></a>
### func [MatchOr](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/predicate.go#L92>)

```go
func MatchOr(preds ...Predicate) Predicate
```

MatchOr matches a page when any predicate does \(empty = matches nothing, the dual of MatchAnd\). The first error stops it.

<a name="MatchRegion"></a>
### func [MatchRegion](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/predicate.go#L226>)

```go
func MatchRegion(boxID string, m TextMatcher) Predicate
```

MatchRegion matches templated pages whose transcription of one template box matches. boxID names the box \("" = any of them\); only boxes the page's template declares are considered, a declared box with no section yet reads as empty text, and a non\-templated page never matches.

<a name="MatchTag"></a>
### func [MatchTag](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/predicate.go#L148>)

```go
func MatchTag(m TextMatcher) Predicate
```

MatchTag matches pages with at least one matching snorg\-managed tag — the page's own tags plus the ones inherited from its note \(EffectiveTags\).

<a name="ParseQuery"></a>
### func [ParseQuery](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/querylang.go#L28>)

```go
func ParseQuery(expr string) (Predicate, error)
```

ParseQuery compiles a query expression into a Predicate — the string language behind the CLI's query command \(see QuerySyntax\). The grammar \(AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, terms\) is parsed by internal/querylang; this is where the field vocabulary lives, so an unknown name, a value on a term that takes none or a bad regexp/date is rejected here, with the column it appeared at.

<a name="Provider"></a>
## type [Provider](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/analyze.go#L14-L17>)

Provider is an analysis backend: a vision Transcriber \(page/region image → text\) and a text Generator \(content → field\) in one. Client.NewProvider builds the one the configuration describes; NewOpenAIProvider builds one for any OpenAI\-compatible endpoint from explicit credentials. A caller may pass its own implementation to Analyze instead — that argument is the backend seam.

```go
type Provider interface {
    Transcriber
    Generator
}
```

<a name="NewOpenAIProvider"></a>
### func [NewOpenAIProvider](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/analyze.go#L20>)

```go
func NewOpenAIProvider(endpoint, apiKey, model string) (Provider, error)
```

NewOpenAIProvider builds a Provider backed by an OpenAI\-compatible endpoint.

<a name="TextChangeOf"></a>
### func [TextChangeOf](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/change.go#L15>)

```go
func TextChangeOf(was, now string) TextChange
```

TextChangeOf classifies the transition was → now — new, updated, cleared or unchanged — and carries both texts. It never reports TextReverted: returning to the AI base is a property of a write, not of two texts, so only an edit that lands on the stored base can produce that verdict.

<a name="Exact"></a>
### func [Exact](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/predicate.go#L56>)

```go
func Exact(want string) TextMatcher
```

Exact matches text equal to want \(the '=' operator\).

<a name="Regexp"></a>
### func [Regexp](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/predicate.go#L44>)

```go
func Regexp(re *regexp.Regexp) TextMatcher
```

Regexp matches text the regexp matches anywhere \(the '\~' operator\).

<a name="Substring"></a>
### func [Substring](<https://github.com/jdlugosz963/snorg/blob/main/pkg/snorg/predicate.go#L50>)

```go
func Substring(sub string) TextMatcher
```

Substring matches text containing sub, case\-insensitively \(the ':' operator — the everyday one, which is why it folds case and needs no escaping\).
